ratings.reviewer_notes: Focused review describing sulforaphane-mediated Keap1 cysteine modification, Nrf2 regulation, and ARE-dependent antioxidant gene activation.
Review-level evidence identifies curcumin, quercetin, resveratrol, EGCG, apigenin, sulforaphane, and ursolic acid as NRF2/ARE modulators in oxidative stress-related models.

Systematic review of human interventions involving twelve phytochemicals, including curcumin, resveratrol, and sulforaphane; evidence for Nrf2 activation was limited and not consistently tied to oxidative stress models.
Vitamin E and curcumin reduced oxidative stress in altered-thyroid rat hearts, but NRF2/KEAP1 modulation was inferred mainly from in silico interaction rather than directly demonstrated.
Broad IBD review discusses numerous natural antioxidants and Nrf2 signaling in intestinal oxidative stress, but the abstract does not establish Nrf2 modulation separately for each listed compound.
Direct mouse and H2O2-treated cell evidence shows resveratrol increases Nrf2-HO-1-NQO1 signaling; Nrf2 siRNA prevents its antioxidative effect.
Review compares sulforaphane, curcumin, silymarin, and resveratrol as natural Nrf2 activators affecting cytoprotective and redox-defense genes.
Direct biochemical evidence demonstrates sulforaphane modification of multiple Keap1 cysteines, including C151, supporting its mechanism of Nrf2/ARE activation.
RA-focused review identifies curcumin, resveratrol, sulforaphane, and propolis as natural antioxidants modulating redox-sensitive pathways including Nrf2/HO-1.

Broad neuroprotection review covers EGCG, quercetin, curcumin, resveratrol, rosmarinic acid, carnosic acid, sulforaphane, and allicin; Nrf2 activation is presented as one possible antioxidant mechanism.
Review describes sulforaphane, resveratrol, curcumin, luteolin, corosolic acid, and apigenin as NRF2 activators, emphasizing epigenetic reversal of NRF2 promoter hypermethylation.
Direct H2O2-induced endothelial oxidative stress study shows synergistic curcumin-resveratrol treatment enhances Nrf2 translocation, Nrf2 and HO-1 expression, and antioxidant activity.

Cancer-focused review catalogs twelve nutraceuticals, including curcumin, sulforaphane, resveratrol, lycopene, kaempferol, allicin, thymoquinone, quercetin, gingerol, and piperine, as Keap1-Nrf2 modulators.
Focused review explains how sulforaphane disrupts Keap1-mediated Nrf2 degradation, enabling Nrf2 nuclear accumulation and cytoprotective responses against oxidants.

Bibliometric review provides adjacent evidence by identifying sulforaphane, curcumin, and resveratrol as prominent natural compounds reported to modulate Nrf2, but it does not evaluate individual experiments.
Diabetes-focused review discusses curcumin, sulforaphane, resveratrol, vitamin D, and other natural Nrf2 activators used to mitigate oxidative stress and hyperglycemic injury.
Direct H2O2-induced macrophage oxidative stress study shows curcumin promotes Nrf2 nuclear translocation, HO-1 expression, and antioxidant enzyme activity, with dose-dependent effects.

Direct mechanistic study shows curcumin suppresses inflammatory induction of Keap1 and Nrf2 polyubiquitination, thereby activating Nrf2 and improving redox homeostasis under insulin-resistant conditions.
General mechanistic review names curcumin, quercetin, resveratrol, and sulforaphane as natural Keap1-Nrf2 activators that support protection from oxidants and electrophiles.
Focused review synthesizes evidence for food- and plant-derived Nrf2 activators in experimental stroke models involving oxidative stress, though individual compounds are not named in the abstract.
Direct H2O2-treated rheumatoid synoviocyte study shows resveratrol increases Nrf2 and HO-1, decreases Keap1 and ROS, and loses antioxidant efficacy after Nrf2 silencing.
